question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & \,0\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(\frac{1}{5}<X\,|\,Y=\frac{4}{3}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(X\in A\,|\,Y=y)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{5}<X\,|\,Y=\frac{4}{3}) & ={\int }_{1/5}^{1}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{4}{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/5}^{1}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{1/5}^{1} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{25} \\  & =\frac{24}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
